spec.name: Earnings drift v24
spec.notes: Rank names by the latest earnings surprise and hold through the drift.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.5, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.52 to 2.38 (change -0.14).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.52 to 2.52. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.46 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.52); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.52 against 2.52 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 2.36 against 2.52 in research, a gap of +0.16.
The best year gives 20% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 98%; Sharpe is 3.45 in calm and 0.23 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.50 becomes 2.50 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.33 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.41).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 29% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 19% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
